Equity Quant ML — Analysis Report

S&P 500 market analysis & machine-learning trading signals

Sample: 21 tickers across 8 GICS sectors · 2016-01-04 to 2026-09-18 · 56,553 daily records · generated 2026-09-20 02:28

1. Executive Summary

This project builds an end-to-end quantitative research pipeline over 56,553 daily records for 21 S&P 500 constituents: market data ingestion and caching, an SQLite analytical layer, rigorous cleaning and validation, exploratory analysis, a formal statistical hypothesis-testing suite, technical feature engineering, next-day direction classification with time-series-aware validation, and an out-of-sample backtest net of transaction costs.

Headline finding. The random_forest classifier reaches ROC-AUC 0.530 (accuracy 54.7% vs 54.7% up-period base rate) on out-of-sample data, and the weekly-rebalanced signal improves the SPY buy-and-hold Sharpe by 0.68 (1.962 vs 1.278) net of 2 bps transaction costs.

2. Data & Pipeline Overview

Daily OHLCV bars are pulled from Yahoo Finance (split/dividend adjusted), cached as Parquet, then loaded into a local SQLite warehouse where analytical SQL (window functions, CTEs, joins) produces the aggregates used throughout this report. 3. Exploratory Analysis

4. Statistical Hypothesis Testing

Jarque-Bera rejects normality for 21 of 21 tickers (pooled excess kurtosis = 15.0): daily returns have fat tails, so Gaussian-based risk metrics understate tail risk and non-parametric/tree models are preferred.

ADF on the price-like series of KO: p = 9.34e-01 (unit root NOT rejected -> non-stationary); on daily returns: p = 8.10e-29 (unit root rejected -> stationary). Modelling returns instead of prices is therefore statistically justified.

Ljung-Box on returns at lag 10: p = 0.00e+00; on squared returns: p = 0.00e+00. Returns show little linear memory (weak-form efficiency) while squared returns are strongly autocorrelated -> pronounced volatility clustering (ARCH effects). This motivates the rolling-volatility and Bollinger-band features in the model.

5. Machine Learning — Next-week Direction

27 causal technical features (trailing returns, trend ratios, RSI, MACD, Bollinger statistics, realised volatility, microstructure and cross-sectional ranks, plus sector dummies) feed three classifiers. Labels are the direction of the next 5-trading-day return, sampled every 5 days so labels never overlap. Model selection uses 5-fold time-series cross-validation inside the training period; the final evaluation is on a chronological hold-out (last 20% of dates).

6. Out-of-sample Backtest

The portfolio rebalances every 5 trading days: long positions are taken only when the predicted probability of an up-period reaches 0.55 (vs 0.50 unconditional), with 2 bps charged per unit of turnover. The benchmark is SPY buy-and-hold measured over the identical rebalance windows.

7. Conclusions & Limitations

  • Across time-series cross-validation and the chronological hold-out, tree ensembles extract a modest but consistent edge over the up-period base rate at the weekly horizon; volatility, trend and volume features dominate the importance ranking.
  • The statistical suite confirms fat tails (JB rejected for 21 of 21 tickers), stationary returns, and strong volatility clustering - justifying the feature families chosen for the model.
  • The weekly-rebalanced, probability-threshold strategy delivers Sharpe 1.962 vs 1.278 for SPY with max drawdown -10.79% vs -13.98%, at 79.1% average exposure - the selective positioning (staying in cash when confidence is low) is the main source of drawdown reduction.
  • Limitations. Directional accuracy above the coin-flip level is modest and consistent with weak-form market efficiency; the edge is thin and sensitive to cost assumptions. The universe is limited to 21 large caps, labels are close-dated with no overnight-gap separation, and no regime-switching or macro features are included. This is a research artefact demonstrating methodology, not investment advice.
Data: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (split/dividend adjusted). Generated by the Equity Quant ML pipeline (Python, pandas, scikit-learn, XGBoost, SQLite, statsmodels). For research/educational use only.
